key_insight: Wall curvature reorganizes supersonic turbulence: concave walls promote structured triadic energy transfers and vortex breakdown, while convex walls suppress redistribution and retain energy in elongated streamwise streaks.
engineering_relevance: Distinguishing nonlinear scale selection from linear structure formation can inform turbulence modeling and flow-control strategies for curved supersonic surfaces.
method: Direct numerical simulations of supersonic turbulent boundary layers over concave and convex walls.
Scale-resolved TKE budgets, triadic transfer bispectra, and spectral proper orthogonal decomposition.
Global resolvent analysis to identify linear amplification and mean-flow receptivity.
evidence_signal: The analyses identify concave-wall outer-layer production at low spanwise wavenumbers and multi-step triadic transfer—not a three-dimensional inverse cascade—alongside convex-wall suppression of pressure-strain redistribution.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish generality across Mach numbers, Reynolds numbers, or curvature strengths, so engineering extrapolation requires validation.
paper_title: Triadic energy cascades and linear amplification mechanisms in supersonic turbulent boundary layers over curved walls
